newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM considers U.N. complaint against co-PM.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM considers U.N. complaint against co-PM.

text.p: The rocky relationship between Cambodia's co-premiers worsened on Thursday after Prince Norodom Ranariddh appeared set to file a complaint at the United Nations against fellow leader Hun Sen.
Hun Sen responded by continuing his attacks on the monarchy, the subject which has spurred their current feud. He challenged Ranariddh to follow through with his threats.
"The past bitterness of Cambodian history has returned," Hun Sen warned in an angry speech broadcast on the radio.
On Thursday, Ranariddh's advisers confirmed reports he was considering filing a complaint against Hun Sen with the U.N. Commission on Human Rights in Geneva, but declined to give details.
Observers said the complaint appeared linked to Hun Sen's recent attacks on the monarchy.

Hun Sen has vowed to ask King Norodom Sihanouk to ban royal family members from politics unless they renounced their royal status and warned he would cancel coming elections if the king abdicated to enter politics.

Hun Sen said on Thursday he would ask all parties to sign an agreement to hold local and national elections as scheduled in 1997 and 1998. But if a crisis emerged over the monarachy, elections would be postponed.
Ranariddh's threat to bring his complaints to the United Nations appeared ironic. It was U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993 that led to the current uneasy coalition government.
Their relationship has deteriorated steadily ahead of the upcoming polls which will pit their two parties against each other.
The controversy has spilled over to television and radio stations separately controlled by the two leaders.

Khmer Rouge radio, the mouthpiece of the hardline rebels who led the brutal 1975-1979 "killing fields" regime, also jumped into the fray with a statement condemning Hun Sen and the CPP and volunteering to marshall their forces to protect royalists.
